recommended_rollout.canonical_core: Implement the provider-neutral outbound transactional message aggregate before any live channel adapter.
recommended_rollout.channel_a: Evolution API v2.3.7 using only WHATSAPP-BAILEYS linked-device instances, explicitly identified as a non-official connection, with pairing, multiple Organization-scoped channels, send_text, delivery receipts, and status reconciliation behind disabled effects.
recommended_rollout.channel_b: Direct WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API using approved utility templates as the official WhatsApp alternative, isolated from Evolution linked-device sessions.
recommended_rollout.channel_c: Transactional email through Amazon SES after the two WhatsApp adapters, with multipart text/HTML templates and authenticated SES/SNS delivery feedback.
recommended_rollout.deferred_channels: Evolution Go, WAHA, SMS, inbound conversations, campaigns, marketing automation, chatbot, AI-generated content, attachments, voice, social inbox, and additional providers remain deferred.
recommended_rollout.production_effects: No production credential, real recipient, public webhook subscription, provider template creation, sender-domain change, sandbox call, or provider enablement belongs to planning or ordinary implementation/CI.

evolution_api_v2_3_7_linked_device.rule: A configured secret webhook header authenticates possession of a shared secret but is not represented as a payload-bound cryptographic signature.

provider_capability_contract.rule: Services branch on declared capability rather than provider name; unsupported operations fail canonically and never fall back automatically.

expected_models.name: Message
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped canonical outbound transactional message aggregate bound to one approved source event or an explicit approved manual source, closed template version, channel, minimized recipient snapshot, lifecycle, and version.

expected_models.name: MessageDeliveryAttempt
expected_models.purpose: One serialized provider attempt for a Message, with leases, controlled retry evidence, sanitized external identifiers, and no raw provider body or credential.

expected_models.name: MessageTemplate
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped, versioned, immutable-after-use template definition with semantic key, channel, locale, approved parameter schema, provider template reference, and no arbitrary runtime code.

expected_models.name: MessagingProviderConnection
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped provider installation/account configuration, connection mode, capability snapshot, and opaque secret aliases. It distinguishes Evolution linked-device, Meta official, and SES without exposing provider concepts in Message.

expected_models.name: MessagingChannel
expected_models.purpose: One Organization-scoped sender channel or Evolution instance under a provider connection, with provider-neutral lifecycle, external channel identifier, capability snapshot, and per-channel opaque credential alias. Pairing material is never persisted.

expected_models.name: MessagingPreference
expected_models.purpose: Customer/contact/channel/purpose permission or suppression record with provenance, policy version, effective time, and immutable history sufficient to fail closed before dispatch.

expected_models.name: MessageAutomationRule
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped mapping from an allowlisted internal event to one template and channel, disabled by default and versioned for deterministic event consumption.

expected_models.name: MessageStatusHistory
expected_models.purpose: Immutable canonical transition history separate from AuditEvent and provider callback evidence.

expected_models.name: MessageCommandReceipt
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped idempotency receipt for every mutable Messaging command.

expected_models.name: MessageWebhookReceipt
expected_models.purpose: Authenticated and deduplicated delivery-status evidence containing only channel, account, external event/message identifiers, digest, canonical result, and timestamps; never a raw callback.

expected_features: Create outbound transactional messages only from an allowlisted approved event or an explicit manual command tied to an approved Order, Fulfillment, or Payment source; arbitrary free-text and marketing sends are forbidden.

Use versioned closed templates and allowlisted variables, rendering only at dispatch while preserving a minimized deterministic parameter snapshot and never persisting a raw provider request or response.

Support manual sending of an active hosted checkout link and event-driven Order confirmation, Fulfillment progress, Payment paid, and checkout-link availability behind independently configurable rules disabled by default.

Dispatch asynchronously through transactional outbox and the integrations Celery queue, with network I/O outside transactions, leases, backoff, deterministic locks, and fail-closed handling of ambiguous provider acceptance.

Expose provider-neutral adapters for Evolution API v2.3.7 linked-device text messaging, direct WhatsApp Cloud API utility templates, and Amazon SES transactional email behind disabled external effects and offline contract fixtures.

Create, inspect, pair, reconcile, and disconnect Evolution linked-device channels through explicit manager commands; QR and pairing codes are ephemeral secret responses and never persisted, logged, audited, or emitted.

Accept delivery-status callbacks only through channel-account-scoped endpoints, authenticate them, deduplicate them, discard raw PII, and map out-of-order provider evidence monotonically to canonical states.
Enforce active contact, explicit per-purpose messaging permission, customer-merge handling, suppression, channel/template compatibility, and source freshness immediately before dispatch.
Provide organization-scoped selectors, manager configuration, operator manual send using approved templates, masked visibility, server-rendered HTML, audit, and sanitized internal outbox events.

states.requirement: Proposed canonical lifecycle requiring explicit human approval before implementation.
states.rule: Provider statuses are mapped by adapters and never copied into Message.status. sent means provider acceptance, not recipient delivery. uncertain is non-terminal and only verified reconciliation or an explicit manager decision after preserved evidence may resolve it.
states.monotonicity: Authenticated callbacks may arrive duplicated or out of order. delivered cannot regress; read is intentionally not canonical; late failed evidence after delivered is retained as sanitized evidence and surfaced for attention rather than silently rewriting delivery.
states.single_active_attempt: At most one requested, sending, accepted, or uncertain attempt may exist per Message. Channel/provider fallback is never automatic.

manual_use_cases: send the currently active hosted checkout link
rules: Every automatic rule is Organization-scoped, disabled by default, and consumes only the exact allowlisted event version.
The consumer re-fetches and revalidates the source aggregate in the same Organization; sanitized event payloads are routing evidence, never authorization or message content.

Payment-link dispatch locks and revalidates the exact active PaymentAttempt immediately before send; stale, cancelled, expired, replaced, cross-Organization, or requires_attention payment links block dispatch.
Customer merge never silently repoints a pending message. Dispatch is blocked until an authorized user selects the canonical Customer and active ContactPoint explicitly.
Order, Fulfillment, and Payment canonical states are never changed by Messaging.

snapshots: Message stores source type/id/version, template id/version, channel, locale, customer display name, exact ContactPoint id and normalized destination, purpose, permission evidence id, and only allowlisted scalar template parameters under a closed versioned schema.

The hosted checkout URL may be resolved from the exact active PaymentAttempt at dispatch and must not be copied into AuditEvent, OutboxEvent, MessageCommandReceipt, logs, metrics, callback receipts, or exception text.

Rendered bodies, raw provider requests/responses, inbound content, documents, addresses, notes, tokens, signatures, credentials, provider diagnostics, tracking pixels, and arbitrary metadata are not persisted.
OPERATOR views a masked destination and canonical delivery state; OWNER, ADMIN, and MANAGER may view the full destination and sanitized provider evidence required for operations.
AuditEvent and OutboxEvent contain canonical IDs, semantic template key, channel, purpose, state, version, and boolean reason flags only.
idempotency: Every mutable local command uses MessageCommandReceipt scoped by Organization, operation, and idempotency key with canonical payload hashing.
Automatic creation is unique by Organization, source event id, automation-rule version, template version, channel, and destination snapshot so outbox replay cannot duplicate a message.
Each outbound attempt has one stable internal dispatch key and provider correlation tag; retries reuse the same attempt only when the adapter contract proves retry safety.
A timeout or transport loss after possible acceptance on a provider without an idempotent send contract becomes uncertain and is never blindly resent.
External message and event IDs are unique per MessagingProviderConnection and MessagingChannel scope and never trusted globally without Organization and channel correlation.
Webhook receipts deduplicate authenticated events and apply only monotonic transitions; duplicate and out-of-order status callbacks are safe.
Network I/O occurs outside database transactions; leases and deterministic lock order prevent simultaneous sends of the same Message.
money_rules: Messaging never computes, changes, rounds, discounts, surcharges, or persists a new financial amount.
If an approved template displays money, the value and BRL currency come from the immutable approved Order or Payment snapshot and are formatted only for presentation.
A checkout link is sent only for the exact active PaymentAttempt whose intent amount and currency were already validated by Payments.
Provider messaging fees, WhatsApp conversation charges, email costs, budgets, billing, and accounting remain outside canonical Order and Payment totals.
permission_and_privacy: MessagingPreference records permission or suppression for one active ContactPoint, channel, transactional purpose, provenance, policy version, and effective time; missing or stale evidence fails closed.

The Organization remains responsible for selecting and documenting an applicable LGPD legal basis. Vidalys Flow records evidence and enforces the decision but does not infer legal basis from a contact existing in Customers.

A customer or channel opt-out, hard bounce, complaint, inactive contact, merged customer, or invalid endpoint blocks future dispatch for that scope; transactional necessity does not authorize silent override.
Marketing purpose is structurally unavailable in Phase 06. Transactional templates cannot contain promotions or arbitrary free text.
Data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, correction, opposition, suppression, and deletion/anonymization procedures must be documented and directly tested where technically applicable.
provider_and_webhook_security: Provider credentials live only in an approved secret channel and are referenced by opaque aliases; they never enter models, fixtures, logs, CI, handoffs, or Git.
Evolution API is pinned for implementation planning to stable v2.3.7 and only WHATSAPP-BAILEYS linked-device mode. It is operationally labeled non-official and is never presented as Meta Cloud API.

Evolution connection management uses deterministic instance identity, one per-channel secret alias, ephemeral QR/pairing responses, HTTPS, exact deploy host allowlists, DNS/IP validation against SSRF, no embedded credentials, no redirects, explicit timeout, and no HTTP retry.

Evolution v2.3.7 documents instance/global API keys and arbitrary webhook headers but not a payload-bound cryptographic signature or send idempotency key. A distinct per-connection webhook secret header, constant-time comparison, HTTPS, account/channel correlation, replay deduplication, and Security Review are mandatory before callback activation.

Evolution subscribes only to the minimum delivery-status event needed. Inbound messages, contacts, chats, presence, history sync, QR updates, media bodies, and API keys received in webhook payloads are discarded and never persisted.

An Evolution send timeout without a returned provider message ID becomes uncertain. Status query is allowed only when the exact channel and message ID exist and the adopted installation contract supports message persistence; absence of a record never proves failure.

WhatsApp sends only approved utility templates through the official Cloud API; external message IDs are stored only for correlation and status webhooks are treated as potentially duplicated and out of order.

Amazon SES sends one recipient per canonical Message using a verified sender identity and message tags for correlation; provider acceptance is not delivery and ambiguous send errors are not blindly retried.

Evolution, Meta Cloud, and SES/SNS callbacks remain disabled until their authenticity contracts are implemented and independently reviewed. SNS requires signature verification, trusted HTTPS certificate origin, expected TopicArn, timestamp/replay checks, and SignatureVersion2 where configured.
Callback bodies and headers are size-limited, processed ephemerally, never logged or persisted raw, and reduced to allowlisted canonical evidence after authentication.
Public callback endpoints use HTTPS, strict methods/content types, rate limits, generic responses, account-derived Organization, and no caller-supplied Organization authorization.
Open, click, and read tracking are not canonical and are not collected in this phase. Inbound WhatsApp message bodies are rejected or discarded without persistence.
authorization: Organization for human commands comes from authenticated active Membership and is never accepted as a free request identifier.

OWNER, ADMIN, MANAGER, and OPERATOR may list messages, view masked canonical status, and manually request an enabled approved transactional template for an eligible source and active permitted contact.

Only OWNER, ADMIN, and MANAGER may configure provider connections/channels, request Evolution pairing, templates, automation rules, preferences/suppressions, retry or cancel sends, reconcile uncertain cases, and view full destinations or sanitized provider evidence.
No role may create arbitrary free text, bypass an inactive contact or suppression, change a source aggregate, or activate external effects through the application.
Automatic consumers and workers revalidate Organization, rule version, permission, ContactPoint, source aggregate, template, and channel account before dispatch.
Every selector, service, worker, callback, and admin surface has direct cross-organization tests.

acceptance_criteria: The complete transactional-only scope, channels, source allowlist, states, permission evidence, templates, roles, retry ambiguity, and deferred scope are explicitly approved before implementation.
The implementation starts exactly from actual_base_sha 3e4fcfb064fbee350d3df131b2946974c8557098 and depends on approved Phase 05 head 3558ca30a5652be320feb3f28ab46a350ae9cad7.

The explicitly authorized Flowlog consultation remains limited to the frozen SHA and recorded Messaging paths; no code, model, migration, data, ID, credential, endpoint, template, contact, runtime, provider configuration, machine, or infrastructure is copied or linked.
Every message belongs to Organization, an approved source/template/channel/purpose, exact active ContactPoint, and valid permission evidence; missing evidence fails closed.
Only one active attempt exists per Message and an ambiguous provider result is surfaced rather than retried into a possible duplicate.
Payment links are resolved and revalidated against the exact active PaymentAttempt immediately before dispatch; stale links never send silently.
Callback authenticity, channel-account scope, deduplication, replay protection, out-of-order monotonicity, PII disposal, and suppression are enforced and directly tested.
No provider network call occurs in request transactions or CI; external effects remain disabled without separately approved sandbox or production activation.
Organization isolation, authorization, masking, idempotency, expected_version, deterministic locks, template immutability, and sanitization are enforced and tested.
All gates and CI pass on the candidate HEAD, independent Review has no unresolved blocker, and QA/Security emits GO.
Human approval remains explicit before implementation, sandbox access, PR, merge, release, provider enablement, deploy, state approval, or the next phase.
human_decisions_required: Approve transactional outbound Messaging only, with marketing, campaigns, inbound conversations, chatbot, AI content, SMS, and attachments deferred.

Approve Evolution API stable v2.3.7 linked-device as WhatsApp provider A, direct WhatsApp Cloud API utility templates as the official WhatsApp provider B, and Amazon SES as email provider C, all disabled by default and tested offline.

Approve Evolution as explicitly non-official, with per-Organization instances/channels, ephemeral pairing, no inbound content, no media in this phase, and no production use before separate Security and infrastructure approval.
Approve the automatic event allowlist and that every automation rule starts disabled per Organization; manual sends must also reference an approved source and template.
Approve that ContactPoint existence alone is insufficient: each dispatch requires active endpoint plus recorded per-purpose permission evidence, and suppression always fails closed.

Approve OWNER, ADMIN, MANAGER, and OPERATOR for approved manual sends, with configuration, automation, retries, reconciliation, preferences, full destinations, and evidence restricted to manager tier.

Approve pending, queued, sending, sent, delivered, failed, cancelled, and uncertain as Message states plus inactive, connecting, pairing_required, active, degraded, disconnected, and disabled as channel states; provider read/open/click signals remain outside the canonical lifecycle.
Approve no blind retry after ambiguous provider acceptance and no automatic channel/provider fallback.
Approve that implementation and CI use fakes/contract fixtures only; sandbox, public callbacks, real recipients, DNS/sender changes, and production effects require later explicit authorization.
